channel.title: Scotti's Corner
channel.description: Notes from Scotti, who builds ScottiCAD.

item.title: Your first ScottiCAD script
item.description: Get started by writing your very first script in ScottiCAD. Its scripting language is a variant of Python with a gentle learning curve that even novices can use to make parametric models.

item.title: Putting text on your 3D prints
item.description: Sometimes you want to add labels, part numbers or a version indicator to a 3D print. This post shows how to do it, raised or engraved, helps you pick a font, and gives you some guidelines on font size.

item.title: Three tools for people who actually print
item.description: Look inside a part, lay it flat for printing, and see what it'll cost in filament, all without leaving the CAD program.

item.title: Raspberry Pi mounts that line up the first time
item.description: Standoffs, a plate, and a see-through Pi on top that shows exactly where every port goes. Then I drop it in a case and let it cut the openings for me.

item.title: How I build a project box
item.description: The project box from my first post, step by step: a box, a hole, a lid, four screw posts, and countersunk holes for M3 screws.

item.title: Why I wrote ScottiCAD
item.description: My designs lived in somebody else's cloud, until an update broke half a dozen of them. So I built a CAD program that runs on my own computer.
